text:
Staff briefings at dusk brought a puzzling request for the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. Routine checks had just been finished when a traveler arrived with a pet booking that did not match the flight file. The traveler said the animal had already been accepted for carriage, yet the desk record showed no confirmed handoff to the cabin team. I reviewed the booking notes, checked the transfer list, and compared the animal care instructions against the departure packet. The file showed a clean reservation, but the custody trail was incomplete, so the case was treated as an operational mismatch rather than a service complaint.

I spoke with the gate team and the loading lead to confirm whether the carrier had been scanned at acceptance. No scan could be found in the active system, and the manifest copy at the desk did not show a final release note. I then contacted the cabin team and reminded them that every animal receives patient attention from trained staff and that the handling notes must travel with the pet at each handoff. The crew checked the cabin bay, confirmed the pet was stable, and reported no welfare issue. The animal remained calm throughout the review, and the traveler waited in the customer area while the file was corrected.

After the discrepancy was narrowed down, I updated the desk log, reissued the care summary, and sent the practical instructions to the crew station. The traveler was advised that the pet would continue under normal monitoring and that the escort record would be reconciled before the next transfer point. The gate and cabin teams were reminded to use the same confirmation steps for all companion animals, even on routine turns, so that a missing handoff does not delay movement or create doubt about animal welfare.

Follow-up will focus on the transfer path and the receipt check at the desk. The next shift was told to watch for similar gaps, especially when a booking looks complete but the movement trail is thin. The handling was resolved without distress to the animal, and the record now reflects the correct chain of care.
